paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese; here the whole page body is a substituent enumeration table whose cells are chemical symbols and compound numbers, with no German prose in them at all, so zh and en are the same string. The page carries no Tabelle caption: the table begins on an earlier page and continues past this one, so the shared substituents and the drawn scaffold that govern these rows are not on this page. The column headers are printed with superscript locants (R with superscript 7a, 7b, 12 and 1); they are transcribed inline as R7a, R7b, R12 and R1 because the plain-text transcription has no superscripts, and likewise the subscript digits in SO2, CH2 and CH2CH2 are printed as subscripts and written inline here. Every row on this page has L = CH2CH2. Rows 152 to 173 have R1 = O-c-Hexyl, continuing the block that began at row 150 on the previous page; rows 174 to 178 start a new block with R1 = O-c-Pentyl, which continues past the foot of the page. 'Pr' in PrSO2 is printed with no n- or i- prefix and is transcribed as printed, not resolved to n-propyl; 'Bz' likewise is transcribed as printed and not expanded. A small stray ink mark sits directly above the O of O-c-Hexyl in the R1 cell of row 153, and a faint dot sits in the blank right-hand part of the R12 cell of the same row; a faint tick sits just right of the number in the Nr. cell of row 172. All three are scan artifacts, not characters. The R12 entry of row 169 is printed slightly indented within its cell relative to the rows above and below it, which is a typesetting artifact and not part of the substituent. The cell dividing rules between the R7b and R12 columns and between the L and R1 columns print as broken dotted lines on several rows, which is a print quality artifact and does not affect the cell contents. Below row 178 the lower third of the page is blank.
